title: Exodus wallet vault
whyItMatters: Exodus stores an encrypted vault with the private keys for the person's coins. With the password it is the money; without it, it still proves what they owned.
source: Elastic detection-rules macOS wallet paths reference ~/Library/Application Support/Exodus - https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/issues/6616
notes: Contains the encrypted exodus.wallet vault and timestamped backups. Unconfirmed (no Mac to test): macOS 27 may block this folder with com.apple.macl; no file is opened.

cleanup.exportFirst: Use the recovery phrase screens in Exodus to write down the phrase for each wallet, and store the paper somewhere safe.
steps: Confirm you have the recovery phrase or backup for every wallet in the app.
Quit Exodus so the vault is not in use.
Delete the Exodus folder named in the plan, then empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: The encrypted vault and its backups leave this Mac. The funds are recoverable only with the recovery phrase.
cleanup.source: Exodus, How do I delete my wallet and start over?: https://support.exodus.com/support/en/articles/8598644-how-do-i-delete-my-wallet-and-start-over
